headline: The lost-wallet card handling can be worked out from the documents, but the grade also depends on the agent freezing the cards before closing them, which the documents don't require.

issues.summary: Freezing a lost/stolen card leaves 'frozen_date' and 'unfrozen_date' fields on the card record, and a frozen card must be unfrozen before close_debit_card_4721 will accept it, so the final DB depends on whether the agent froze first. Doc 026 tells agents to recommend closing instead of freezing once loss/theft is confirmed, which gives a second defensible path with a different final state.
evidence: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_026: "If customer confirms the card is lost/stolen, recommend closing instead of freezing"
tools.py freeze_debit_card_3892: card["frozen_date"] = get_today_str(); unfreeze_debit_card_3893: card["unfrozen_date"] = get_today_str()
tools.py close_debit_card_4721: "Only ACTIVE or PENDING cards can be closed."
task_078 instructions step 1: "I need to freeze all of them right away and get replacements."
Replay check: gold minus freeze/unfreeze for dbc_mc78a5b9d2_lb/_green gives a different agent and user DB hash
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that follows doc 026, recommends closing outright, and gets the simulated customer's agreement (the script says to follow the agent's guidance) closes the cards without the freeze/unfreeze round trip. Its card records then lack the two date fields and the unfreeze tool is never logged, so the hash differs from gold. A replay that drops the freeze/unfreeze calls for the closed cards confirmed the mismatch for task_078. The customer's explicit opening request to freeze makes the gold path the usual one, so this is rated Minor.
issues.suggested_fix: Exclude transient freeze bookkeeping fields (frozen_date/unfrozen_date) from the hash, or have close_debit_card_4721 accept FROZEN cards and clear those fields, so both paths converge.

solution_check: I worked through it on my own: verify, then freeze all three cards because the customer asks. Then read transactions: Light Green chk_mc78a5b9d2_3 has two pending rows (btxn_9034c8e42248, btxn_3e4b057911a1), so per doc 025 req 4 it cannot be closed. Light Blue has two 'lost' replacements in 12 months (03/15/2025 and 07/25/2025), so it hits the ENTRY limit of 2 and the customer declines the $25 fee. Green is MID tier (tier names from doc 005), so it gets EXPEDITED $15 with CLASSIC $0. That leaves unfreeze+close for LB and Green (reason 'lost') and one EXPEDITED order for Green. This matches gold, and gold replays without errors.
prior_note: The prior review rated this task clean. The #402 change only added a gold read of get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847, which an agent must call anyway. The freeze-path residue is newly reported here.
notes: Grading-model facts confirmed against the v1.0.1 snapshot: EnvironmentEvaluator replays gold on a fresh env and compares get_db_hash/get_user_db_hash (both hash the same TransactionalDB here because KnowledgeUserTools shares the agent db); _derive_read_log_allowlist logs discoverable reads only when the gold calls that tool name; the agent_discoverable_tools record id is derived from the tool name only, so the log is a set (call count and arguments do not matter), and write-tool calls are logged even when the tool returns an 'Error:' string; call_discoverable_agent_tool parses arguments with json.loads(parse_int=float); get_now() is fixed at 2025-11-14 03:40. Doc 029 names tiers without defining which accounts belong to each. The only checking-account tier mapping is in doc 005 (account closure), which is in required_documents, and agents must apply it to debit-card replacement by analogy. ENTRY tier also has a 48-hour post-closure wait (doc 029), so Light Blue could not be reordered today even with the fee. get_credit_card_accounts_by_user (gold[7]) is a non-discoverable read with no DB effect; the user has no credit cards.
